title: Title & Registration Services Extension Tags: Allowance for a Return Still Being Cured
content:
On a Title & Registration Services order, the extension cure allowance looks at the returns dated on the order's most recent return date: it is three days when a fee-shortage return is dated on that date and a registration-fee entry has been collected on the order on or after that date, ten days when no fee-shortage return is dated on that date and a return needing a corrected document from the customer (a missing signature, insurance not verified, emissions not on file or an odometer discrepancy) is, and nothing otherwise. The allowance is a waiting allowance added, in whole days, on top of an extension tag's base validity.

## Records read

- the state rejection entries on the title order, their reasons and dates; the most recent return date is the latest of those dates;
- the state fee entries collected on the title order under the registration fee, and their dates.

## Truth table

| Fee-shortage return dated on the most recent return date | Registration-fee entry collected on or after that date | Corrected-document return dated on the most recent return date | Cure allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | either | 3 days |
| yes | no | either | nothing |
| no | not relevant | yes | 10 days |
| no | not relevant | no | nothing |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- The latest return, dated 6 May, is for a fee shortage, and a registration-fee entry was collected on 8 May: 3 days.
- The latest return, dated 6 May, is for a fee shortage, and the only registration-fee entry dates from the opening of the order in March: nothing.
- The latest return, dated 6 May, is for insurance not verified, and no fee-shortage return is dated 6 May: 10 days.
- The latest return is for a lien information error only: nothing.
